chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Allah, Exalted and Glorious, forbade usury so that people would not refrain from doing good deeds.

key_terms.اَلْمَعْرُوفِ: Good deeds / Kindness / What is customary
key_terms.اِصْطِنَاعِ: Doing / Performing (specifically good deeds or kindness)

ai.seo_question: What is the wisdom behind the prohibition of usury in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates that the prohibition of riba serves as a social safeguard to preserve the flow of generosity (istina' al-ma'ruf), preventing wealth hoarding from stifling mutual benevolence. This perspective, recorded in al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, highlights the ethical dimension of usury as a barrier to social cohesion rather than merely a financial transaction. It underscores the Shia scholarly view that economic laws are designed to foster a community characterized by active kindness and shared prosperity.
